items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: I feel in my own heart that the dear Lord above put me on this earth to be the Count Basie drummer. And I was so blessed to have that opportunity to play with the Count.

ctx.x: Well, after that when I was twenty years old Louie Bellson had a lot to do with getting me to be Sammy Davis Jr.’s drummer, and I was with Sammy for three years off and on at that point. And to back up one of the greatest showmen of all-time, and what was great is that all his arrangements sounded like the Count Basie band and we just had like forty strings included, and as I said before, that too was one of the great jobs to be paid to learn. You know because when you have to back up the great Sammy Davis, but…

only to their opinion. But the main thing is that I kept my eyes on the Count at all times and he gave me all the cues, you know, whether it was a wink of the eye or a little pinky here, or just a shrug of the shoulder, or anything, I knew what he wanted. And he taught me so much. He didn’t even have to say anything, he just had to look at me you know. And I feel in my own heart that the dear Lord above put me on this earth to be the Count Basie drummer. And I was so blessed to have that opportunity to play with…
Yeah. It’s an awesome responsibility to be in that rhythm section. Who was playing bass at that time?
